WSL + ROS 2 Humble Setup Guide

1. Install WSL
Open Windows PowerShell as Administrator.

Install WSL using:

wsl --install

Restart Windows if requested.

List available Linux distributions:

wsl --list --online

2. Install Ubuntu 22.04

Install Ubuntu 22.04:

wsl --install -d Ubuntu-22.04

Launch Ubuntu and create a Linux username and password.

Verify installed distributions from Windows PowerShell:

wsl --list --verbose

Launch the correct distribution:

wsl -d Ubuntu-22.04

Verify Ubuntu:

lsb_release -a

Expected: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, codename jammy.

3. Update Ubuntu and configure the locale

Run inside Ubuntu 22.04:

sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

Install locale tools:

sudo apt install locales -y

Generate the UTF-8 locale:

sudo locale-gen en_US.UTF-8

Configure the locale:

sudo update-locale LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 LANG=en_US.UTF-8

Set the current terminal's language:

export LANG=en_US.UTF-8

Verify:

locale

4. Enable the required repository

Run:

sudo apt install software-properties-common -y

sudo add-apt-repository universe

5. Add the official ROS 2 package repository

Install curl:

sudo apt update && sudo apt install curl -y

Download the ROS signing key:

sudo curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ros/rosdistro/master/ros.key -o /usr/share/keyrings/ros-archive-keyring.gpg

Add the repository:

echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/ros-archive-keyring.gpg] http://packages.ros.org/ros2/ubuntu $(. /etc/os-release && echo $UBUNTU_CODENAME) main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ros2.list > /dev/null

Update the package list:

sudo apt update

6. Install ROS 2 Humble

Inside Ubuntu 22.04, run:

sudo apt install ros-humble-desktop -y

Verify the installation:

ls /opt/ros

Expected output:

humble

7. Configure the ROS 2 environment

Load ROS 2 manually:

source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash

Check the distribution:

echo $ROS_DISTRO

Expected output:

humble

To load ROS 2 automatically in future Bash terminals, check whether the setup command is already in .bashrc:

grep -n 'source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash' ~/.bashrc

If no matching line appears, add it:

echo "source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash" >> ~/.bashrc

Apply the configuration:

source ~/.bashrc

Verify again:

echo $ROS_DISTRO

8. Open the ROS 2 project in VS Code

The project folder is:

C:\Users\Raghav Sathe\Desktop\R\Projects\Individuals\ROS 2

Its equivalent path inside Ubuntu is:

/mnt/c/Users/Raghav Sathe/Desktop/R/Projects/Individuals/ROS 2

Navigate to the folder:

cd "/mnt/c/Users/Raghav Sathe/Desktop/R/Projects/Individuals/ROS 2"

Open VS Code:

code .

Verify that VS Code is connected to Ubuntu 22.04 through WSL.

9. Reopen the environment later
Open Windows PowerShell.

Launch Ubuntu 22.04:

wsl -d Ubuntu-22.04

Navigate to the project folder:

cd "/mnt/c/Users/Raghav Sathe/Desktop/R/Projects/Individuals/ROS 2"

Open VS Code:

code .

Open a terminal using Terminal → New Terminal.

Verify ROS 2:

echo $ROS_DISTRO

Expected output:

humble

10. Common errors and fixes

Error: wsl: command not found

Cause: A Windows WSL command was entered inside Ubuntu.
Fix: Run wsl --list --verbose in Windows PowerShell.

Error: /opt/ros does not exist

Cause: ROS 2 is not installed in the current Ubuntu distribution.
Fix: Confirm the distribution using lsb_release -a. Install ROS 2 in the correct compatible distribution.

Error: setup.bash: No such file or directory

Cause: The setup file path is incorrect or ROS 2 is not installed.
Correct path for Humble: /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash

Error: echo $ROS_DISTRO prints nothing

Cause: The ROS 2 environment has not been sourced in the current terminal, or ROS 2 is not installed.
Fix: Run source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash, then check again.

Error: VS Code terminal shows MINGW64 or UCRT64

Cause: The terminal is running Git Bash rather than Ubuntu.
Fix: Connect VS Code to Ubuntu-22.04 through WSL and open a new terminal.

Error: cd reports No such file or directory

Cause: The path is incorrect or the folder does not exist.
Fix: Check the Windows folder path and use the equivalent /mnt/c/... path inside Ubuntu.
